rationale:
What I kept, changed and why, in response to the round-1 critique.

Accepted: (1) Speed is the largest risk. Finishing gives 500 points plus a time bonus, and a run that times out at 300 steps scores far less, so the baseline base_speed of 1.4 is too conservative. I raise base_speed to 1.7 (base PWM about 3480, 85 percent). The PWM-to-ground-speed mapping is not given, so this is a judgement, not a calculation. I expect the higher demand to shorten the run, but it may also reduce line-following margin on tight bends. (2) Sensor coverage: the footprint gap is 0.008 m and the tape is 0.025 m, so the line is always seen by at least one sensor. Only the centre sensor covers a centred tape, and I no longer claim otherwise. (3) Body width: the critique is right that body_width does not change the off-track limit in the allowed range, which is set by the 0.06 m floor. I keep 0.12 m only because it is a neutral, valid value, not for margin. (4) Lead: sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, which is about 30 ms of lead at 1.7 m/s. I raise kd from 0.05 to 0.10 so the controller reacts faster to changes in the signal on bends. (5) Motor mismatch: the critique is right that a fixed left/right mismatch gives a steady offset with ki = 0. I add a small ki = 0.02. With the integral capped at +/-2, its maximum contribution is about 0.02 x 2 x 350 = 14 PWM, so it removes bias slowly without risking windup.

Rejected or kept: I keep kp = 2.0 and the symmetric sensor layout and weights. Nothing in the critique or the inputs shows that kp is wrong, and changing it without telemetry would be guesswork. I keep last_direction for line loss, since it suits curved courses.

Predictions (guesses, not expectations): I expect the robot to complete the development tracks in roughly 2.5 to 3.0 s, with progress near 1, a few line-loss events on the slalom, and rms_error around 0.02 to 0.05 m. If the run times out or leaves the line, the next revision should lower base_speed toward 1.5 before changing kp. If steering_oscillation is high, raise kd further before reducing kp.
